subject: Re: Initial-token delay / p95 regressions — CDN/TLS handshake investigation
messages:
From: Nikola Petrov <nikola@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (urgent) Token latency & error spikes affecting clinical workflows

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

We started seeing sharp increases in first-token latency (TTFT) for our Redwood calls this morning around 08:45 PT. Key metrics from our dashboards: p95 TTFT jumped from ~180ms (baseline) to ~840ms, p99 to ~2.3s. Concurrently, our 5xx error rate rose from 0.1% to ~1.8% and throughput dropped ~15% as clients retried. This is impacting real-time charting in our clinician UI.

Attached: p95_trend_acme_20260525.png and logs_acme_20260525.zip (sample request/response timings and client TLS traces). Our infra team saw a large portion of TLS handshake times stuck in the 300-1500ms range, not the request processing.

We need immediate mitigation — is there a way to route our calls to a different edge region or bypass any CDN path causing long TLS handshakes? Please advise ASAP and include an ETA.

Thanks,
Nikola
Principal Engineer, Acme Health

Cc: Nikola Petrov <nikola@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:08:12 -0700
Subject: Re: (urgent) Token latency & error spikes affecting clinical workflows

Marissa / Evelyn —

Thanks for the heads up, Nikola — I can see the same trend in our global telemetry. Quick summary from the initial triage:
- Correlation looks strong between p95/p99 TTFT regressions and increased TLS handshake durations at the edge (several POPs in us-west/us-east).
- No signs of CPU/GPU saturation on inference workers; backend token generation time is normal.
- Error spike appears to be downstream of the handshake delays (clients timing out / retrying).

Immediate asks:
1) Marissa — can you loop in the CDN/edge ops contact and open an urgent ticket with our provider? Call out SNI/TLS handshake timings and include the attached client traces.
2) Evelyn / Infra — can we temporarily pin Acme to a different edge region (via routing rule) or enable direct origin routing for their API key to bypass problematic POPs? Need feasibility and ETA.
3) Nikola — thanks for the logs; we'll keep you updated.

I'll escalate to Sean for a deeper packet-level look. If we need an emergency rollback with the provider, I'll push for that.

-Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikola Petrov <nikola@acmehealth.com>, Jon Miller <jon.miller@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:44:05 -0700
Subject: Re: (urgent) Token latency & error spikes affecting clinical workflows

Quick update from infra packet capture and edge logs:
- We observed elevated TLS handshake RTTs originating from a subset of our CDN POPs (primarily IAD, SFO, and ORD) starting 2026-05-25 08:30 PT.
- The pattern matches a config change pushed by the CDN provider around the same time: altered SNI routing behavior that caused increased handoffs between edge nodes for certain client IP ranges.
- Sample tcpdump shows SYN->TLS_CLIENT_HELLO delays of 250-1200ms before the server responded; no retransmits indicative of packet loss. This suggests an upstream control-plane routing/regeneration issue rather than our origin.

Mitigations we've initiated:
- Opened high-priority ticket with CDN provider and requested rollback of the config change (ticket PD-83921).
- Created a temporary routing override: Acme API keys now prefer our secondary edge pool (bypassing the affected POPs). This should reduce TTFT for them within 10 minutes of propagation.
- Monitoring: enabled additional TLS handshake traces and will stream metrics to the Acme shared dashboard.

Attachments: tcpdump_snippet_20260526.txt (excerpt with timestamps).

Next steps: if provider cannot rollback quickly, we coordinate a permanent routing policy for high-sensitivity customers to avoid dynamic SNI routing.

-Sean
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sean / Karthik —

Appreciate the fast triage and the temporary routing override. We're still seeing intermittent spikes but things look much better on average; p95 has dropped to ~230ms in the last hour. Can you share an ETA for provider rollback or a longer-term mitigation plan? Our on-call will want a timeline for when this is fully resolved.

Thanks,
Jon Miller
Head of Platform, Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 17:02:23 -0700
Subject: Re: (urgent) Token latency & error spikes affecting clinical workflows — final update

Nikola / Jon —

Final update and next steps:
- Provider rolled back the config change on 2026-05-28 14:10 PT after our escalation; they confirmed the SNI routing rule was the root cause.
- Our routing override has been removed and traffic is on normal path. We validated p95 TTFT for Acme is back to ~190ms and p99 under 700ms during steady traffic. Error rate returned to baseline.
- We've created INF-4721 to formalize a "sensitive-customer routing" policy and added Acme to the initial cohort for explicit pinning during provider control-plane changes.
- Draft postmortem: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/postmortem/rd-acme-2026-05-28 (attached as redwood_postmortem_draft_20260528.md).

Apologies for the customer impact — we'll share the final postmortem and remediation plan by Monday. If you'd like an exec briefing, I can arrange a 30-min sync with our Head of Product and CDN contacts.

Thanks for the patience — and thanks to Sean and Marissa for the rapid response.

-Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
